the-simpsons.description: While working for Fat Tony, Bart gains enough influence with his boss to solve his problems with Principal Skinner--perhaps permanently.

the-simpsons.title: Homer Defined
the-simpsons.description: Homer's averting of a nuclear meltdown earns him employee-of-the-month honors--and a call from Magic Johnson; Milhouse's parents prohibit him from playing with Bart.

the-simpsons.title: Like Father, Like Clown
the-simpsons.description: Bart and Lisa use theological arguments to try to reunite Krusty the Clown and his rabbi father, who disowned Krusty when he turned from rabbi to clown.

the-simpsons.title: Treehouse of Horror II
the-simpsons.description: Maggie uses one of three wishes; a mind-reading Bart rules Springfield; Homer donates his brain to Mr. Burns' science project.

the-simpsons.title: Lisa's Pony
the-simpsons.description: After disappointing Lisa, Homer buys her a pony, solving one problem, but creating others, requiring a second job--at Apu's Kwik-E-Mart.

the-simpsons.title: Saturdays of Thunder
the-simpsons.description: When Homer helps Bart build a soapbox racer, it does little for the car but a lot for their relationship.

the-simpsons.title: Flaming Moe's
the-simpsons.description: Moe steals the drink recipe Homer invented, and the rechristened “Flaming Moe” turns his tavern into a hotspot. When a national franchise wants to buy the recipe, Homer wants revenge.

the-simpsons.title: Burns Verkaufen der Kraftwerk
the-simpsons.description: Burns sells the power plant to a German corporation that doesn't care for Homer's approach to his work.

the-simpsons.title: I Married Marge
the-simpsons.description: A trip down memory lane to the early days of Simpson wedded bliss, when Marge was with child and Homer was without a job.

the-simpsons.title: Radio Bart
the-simpsons.description: Bart fools the town into thinking there's a little boy trapped in a well.

the-simpsons.title: Lisa the Greek
the-simpsons.description: Lisa's ability to pick winning football teams kicks off a strong bond with Homer.

the-simpsons.title: Homer Alone
the-simpsons.description: A stressed Marge vacations alone, leaving Bart and Lisa with Patty and Selma, and Maggie with Homer--until she leaves in search of Marge.

the-simpsons.title: Bart the Lover
the-simpsons.description: Bart's answer to detention from Mrs. Krabappel is to answer her personal ad with letters from a Mr. Wonderful, but his last laugh is more of a guilty whimper.

the-simpsons.title: Homer at the Bat
the-simpsons.description: Burns hires Major League ringers for the plant softball championship.

the-simpsons.title: Separate Vocations
the-simpsons.description: The results from their aptitude tests cause Bart and Lisa to make 180-degree turns in their behavior.

the-simpsons.title: Dog of Death
the-simpsons.description: Santa's Little Helper notices resentment after the Simpsons make sacrifices to fund his life-saving operation.

the-simpsons.title: Colonel Homer
the-simpsons.description: Marge fears a cheatin' heart when a waitress-country singer asks Homer to be her manager.

the-simpsons.title: Black Widower
the-simpsons.description: Bart suspects something rotten when Selma gets engaged to Sideshow Bob.

the-simpsons.title: The Otto Show
the-simpsons.description: Spinal Tap hits Springfield, and Otto the bus driver hits the skids after being fired, taking refuge in the Simpsons' garage.

the-simpsons.title: Bart's Friend Falls in Love
the-simpsons.description: Bart resents Milhouse's new girlfriend; Homer gets the wrong subliminal tape, which has him gaining vocabulary, not losing weight.

the-simpsons.title: Brother, Can You Spare Two Dimes?
the-simpsons.description: Homer's half-brother asks for a loan after Homer is awarded some cash.

the-simpsons.title: Kamp Krusty
the-simpsons.description: Bart leads an uprising at Krusty's summer camp after he and Lisa are subjected to a Dickensian sweatshop.

the-simpsons.title: A Streetcar Named Marge
the-simpsons.description: Marge is cast in a version of "A Streetcar Named Desire," playing Blanche to Ned Flanders' Stanley.

the-simpsons.title: Homer the Heretic
the-simpsons.description: After skipping church one Sunday morning, Homer decides to quit church altogether and spend Sundays worshiping in his own way -- with cigars and beer.

the-simpsons.title: Lisa the Beauty Queen
the-simpsons.description: Homer enters Lisa into the Little Miss Springfield Pageant to help her feel better about her looks. But when she must choose between the title and her integrity, she realizes that confidence comes from within.

the-simpsons.title: Treehouse of Horror III
the-simpsons.description: A Halloween trilogy includes a murderous Krusty doll; a "King Kong" parody; an invasion of zombies unleashed by Bart's incantation.

the-simpsons.title: Itchy & Scratchy: The Movie
the-simpsons.description: Bart is punished by being barred from the Itchy and Scratchy movie.

the-simpsons.title: Marge Gets a Job
the-simpsons.description: Mr. Burns is instantly smitten when Marge takes a job at the nuclear power plant.

the-simpsons.title: New Kid on the Block
the-simpsons.description: Bart has a crush on his new neighbor, a teenage girl who only has eyes for Jimbo Jones. Bart sets out to prove that Jimbo is not as tough as he seems.

the-simpsons.title: Mr. Plow
the-simpsons.description: Homer and Barney become competitors in the snow-plowing business.

the-simpsons.title: Lisa's First Word
the-simpsons.description: While trying to get Maggie to say her first word, Marge and Homer reminisce about Bart's and Lisa's first words.

the-simpsons.title: Homer's Triple Bypass
the-simpsons.description: Homer sees a discount doctor for a coronary bypass.

the-simpsons.title: Marge vs. the Monorail
the-simpsons.description: When Springfield gets a sudden windfall, a charismatic traveling salesman convinces the town to build a monorail.

the-simpsons.title: Selma's Choice
the-simpsons.description: After seeing Aunt Gladys die alone, Aunt Selma wants to get married and have a baby... until she spends a day babysitting Bart and Lisa at Duff Gardens.

the-simpsons.title: Brother from the Same Planet
the-simpsons.description: When Homer neglects Bart once too often, Bart goes to the Big Brother program to get a new father figure. Stung, Homer replaces Bart with a little brother.

the-simpsons.title: I Love Lisa
the-simpsons.description: Chief Wiggum's son has a crush on Lisa after she gives him a Valentine out of pity.

the-simpsons.title: Duffless
the-simpsons.description: After a DUI, Homer swears off beer for a month. Meanwhile, Bart and Lisa's sibling rivalry plays out in the school science fair.

the-simpsons.title: Last Exit to Springfield
the-simpsons.description: Union president Homer fights to keep the dental plan.

the-simpsons.title: So It's Come to This: A Simpsons Clip Show
the-simpsons.description: An April Fools' Day prank provides the jumping-off point for Simpson family flashbacks.

the-simpsons.title: The Front
the-simpsons.description: Lisa and Bart write an Itchy and Scratchy episode; Homer makes up a missing high-school credit.

the-simpsons.title: Whacking Day
the-simpsons.description: Lisa takes a stand against Springfield's annual snake-bashing festival.

the-simpsons.title: Marge in Chains
the-simpsons.description: Overwhelmed by her family's demands during a flu epidemic, Marge accidentally shoplifts at the Kwik-E-Mart and winds up in prison.

the-simpsons.title: Krusty Gets Kancelled
the-simpsons.description: Krusty's Hollywood pals help when his show is canceled after a new star causes his ratings to plummet.

the-simpsons.title: Homer's Barbershop Quartet
the-simpsons.description: Homer recalls when he, Apu, Barney and Principal Skinner became recording icons.

the-simpsons.title: Cape Feare
the-simpsons.description: The Simpsons go incognito to avoid the newly paroled Sideshow Bob, who's out to get Bart.

the-simpsons.title: Homer Goes to College
the-simpsons.description: Homer takes Nuclear Physics 101 at the local college, where he gets a trio of nerdy tutors expelled for extracurricular activities.

the-simpsons.title: Rosebud
the-simpsons.description: Burns longs for a childhood toy that winds up in the grip of Maggie.

the-simpsons.title: Treehouse of Horror IV
the-simpsons.description: Homer sells his soul; Vampire Burns invites the Simpsons for dinner; Bart sees a gremlin damaging his school bus.

the-simpsons.title: Marge on the Lam
the-simpsons.description: Marge's wild night out with neighbor Ruth includes running from the police in Ruth's car, stolen from her ex.

the-simpsons.title: Bart's Inner Child
the-simpsons.description: Springfield emulates Bart after he's praised by a self-help guru.

the-simpsons.title: Boy-Scoutz 'N the Hood
the-simpsons.description: After a reckless Squishee bender with Milhouse, Bart wakes to the shocking realization that he joined the Junior Campers. Lured by pocketknives and knot-tying lessons, Bart assimilates into the group but then must face the father-son rafting trip.

the-simpsons.title: The Last Temptation of Homer
the-simpsons.description: Homer struggles with his attraction to new coworker Mindy, a beautiful engineer whose love for doughnuts is equal to his own.

the-simpsons.title: $pringfield (Or, How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love Legalized Gambling)
the-simpsons.description: Legalized gambling comes to Springfield, and Marge becomes addicted; Robert Goulet entertains at Bart's casino for kids.

the-simpsons.title: Homer the Vigilante
the-simpsons.description: Homer leads a vigilante group to catch the Springfield Cat Burglar, who then robs the museum.

the-simpsons.title: Bart Gets Famous
the-simpsons.description: When an on-air remark catapults Bart to instant stardom, he finds that fame isn't all it's cracked up to be.

the-simpsons.title: Homer and Apu
the-simpsons.description: Homer accompanies Apu to the Kwik-E-Mart home office--in India--after Apu is fired.

the-simpsons.title: Lisa vs. Malibu Stacy
the-simpsons.description: Lisa's outrage over the gender stereotypes reinforced by a new talking doll prompts her to confront the dollmaker.

the-simpsons.title: Deep Space Homer
the-simpsons.description: Homer and Barney compete to be the first "average" American in space.

the-simpsons.title: Homer Loves Flanders
the-simpsons.description: Flanders' extra ticket to the big game makes him Homer's new best friend, a role that sorely tests Flanders' patience.

the-simpsons.title: Bart Gets an Elephant
the-simpsons.description: Bart wins an elephant, but Homer won't let him keep it.

the-simpsons.title: Burns' Heir
the-simpsons.description: Bart is picked to be Burns' heir and moves into the Burns mansion, prompting Homer and Marge to hire a deprogrammer to get him back.

the-simpsons.title: Sweet Seymour Skinner's Baadasssss Song
the-simpsons.description: Bart takes his dog to school, which gets Skinner fired, which in turn leaves Bart missing his archnemesis.

the-simpsons.title: The Boy Who Knew Too Much
the-simpsons.description: Bart can clear Mayor Quimby's nephew of a charge of battery, but only by implicating himself as a hooky player.

the-simpsons.title: Lady Bouvier's Lover
the-simpsons.description: Grandpa Simpson falls for Marge's mother, but loses out to a competitor; Bart gets ripped off shopping at home with Homer's credit card.

the-simpsons.title: Secrets of a Successful Marriage
the-simpsons.description: Homer teaches a class on marriage, but sharing secrets about his own union gets him kicked out of the house.

the-simpsons.title: Bart of Darkness
the-simpsons.description: Stuck in his room with a broken leg, Bart hears a high-pitched scream. When he looks through his telescope, he sees a guilty Ned Flanders burying the evidence.

the-simpsons.title: Lisa's Rival
the-simpsons.description: Lisa feels threatened when a new girl moves to Springfield: Allison is smart, pretty, a great saxophone player and a crack diorama builder. Lisa tries to befriend her new rival, but she's consumed with envy and competitiveness.

the-simpsons.title: Another Simpsons Clip Show
the-simpsons.description: After reading the weepy best-seller The Bridges of Madison County, Marge sits down with the family and recalls romantic moments, along with temptations from her bowling instructor Jacques and Homer's coworker Mindy.

the-simpsons.title: Itchy & Scratchy Land
the-simpsons.description: The family's trip to Itchy & Scratchy Land takes an unexpected turn when high-tech robots malfunction and become violent.

the-simpsons.title: Sideshow Bob Roberts
the-simpsons.description: Mayor Quimby pardons attempted murderer Sideshow Bob, who then runs against Quimby for mayor.

the-simpsons.title: Treehouse of Horror V
the-simpsons.description: Lack of beer and cable TV make Homer a crazed killer; the present is altered by a time-traveling Homer; and Principal Skinner turns detention students into food.

the-simpsons.title: Bart's Girlfriend
the-simpsons.description: Bart learns that the good Reverend Lovejoy's daughter is really bad.

the-simpsons.title: Lisa on Ice
the-simpsons.description: Lisa's surprising ability at hockey spawns jealousy in Bart and a showdown when their teams meet.

the-simpsons.title: Homer Badman
the-simpsons.description: When Homer gropes for a gummy candy stuck to the babysitter's pants, she mistakes his intentions and turns the town against him.

the-simpsons.title: Grampa vs. Sexual Inadequacy
the-simpsons.description: Grandpa's homemade tonic puts life back in the Simpson bedroom, so he and Homer hit the road to sell the stuff.

the-simpsons.title: Fear of Flying
the-simpsons.description: When they try to go on vacation, the family discovers Marge's debilitating fear of flying. Marge consults a psychoanalyst to find the source of her baffling fear.

the-simpsons.title: Homer the Great
the-simpsons.description: Homer joins the secret society of the Stonecutters and is suddenly exalted when the brethren discover his birthmark. The ancient order is shaken to the core by the ineptitude of its new Chosen One.

the-simpsons.title: And Maggie Makes Three
the-simpsons.description: The story of Maggie's birth is told in flashbacks: after Homer quits the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant to pursue his dream of working at a bowling alley, Marge reveals that she is pregnant.

the-simpsons.title: Bart's Comet
the-simpsons.description: When Bart is forced to assist Principal Skinner in early-morning astronomy observations, he discovers a giant comet heading towards Springfield. Facing impending doom, the entire town shows up at the Flanders family bomb shelter.

the-simpsons.title: Homie the Clown
the-simpsons.description: Krusty the Clown's reckless spending forces him to open a clown college to keep afloat. New graduate Homer discovers the perks and perils of being Krusty.

the-simpsons.title: Bart vs. Australia
the-simpsons.description: After tricking an Australian boy into accepting a collect call, Bart flies Down Under to apologize.

the-simpsons.title: Homer vs. Patty and Selma
the-simpsons.description: A loan from Patty and Selma makes Homer their slave; Bart is forced to take ballet.

the-simpsons.title: A Star Is Burns
the-simpsons.description: Film critic Jay Sherman is among the judges at the Springfield Film Festival, which Mr. Burns conspires to win by bribing some judges.

the-simpsons.title: Lisa's Wedding
the-simpsons.description: A fortuneteller predicts Lisa's engagement and wedding to a fellow student from an upper-crust British family.

the-simpsons.title: Two Dozen and One Greyhounds
the-simpsons.description: The Simpson household's overrun with puppies--the offspring of Santa's Little Helper and his new girlfriend from which Mr. Burns would love to make a greyhound-skin tuxedo.

the-simpsons.title: The PTA Disbands
the-simpsons.description: Bart helps precipitate a teachers strike, but he rues his handiwork when Marge takes over for Mrs. Krabappel.

the-simpsons.title: Round Springfield
the-simpsons.description: Bart winds up in the hospital as a result of eating Krusty cereal, and when Lisa comes to visit him, she is reunited with her sax idol.

the-simpsons.title: The Springfield Connection
the-simpsons.description: Marge joins the police force after thwarting a criminal, and Homer thinks he now has a free ride as a cop's spouse.

the-simpsons.title: Lemon of Troy
the-simpsons.description: Springfield boys try to recapture the town's beloved lemon tree after it's stolen.

the-simpsons.title: Who Shot Mr. Burns? (1)
the-simpsons.description: Mr. Burns makes many enemies when he steals the oil discovered beneath Springfield Elementary.

the-simpsons.title: Who Shot Mr. Burns? (2)
the-simpsons.description: With Mr. Burns shot, Chief Wiggum investigates the crime, and nearly everyone in town has a motive. At the end, it all comes down to the Simpson DNA.

the-simpsons.title: Radioactive Man
the-simpsons.description: Bart auditions for the part of Fallout Boy in the movie "Radioactive Man," being filmed in Springfield.

the-simpsons.title: Home Sweet Homediddly-Dum-Doodily
the-simpsons.description: When Homer and Marge are found to be unfit parents, the kids are placed with the Flanders family. Reluctant participants in the Flanderses' wholesome family activities, Bart and Lisa become the targets of an emergency baptism.

the-simpsons.title: Bart Sells His Soul
the-simpsons.description: Bart sells his soul to Milhouse for five dollars, but soon regrets his decision. Meanwhile, Moe turns the Tavern into a family-friendly restaurant.

the-simpsons.title: Lisa the Vegetarian
the-simpsons.description: After visiting a local petting zoo, Lisa becomes a vegetarian and faces ridicule from family and friends. When she lashes out and ruins Homer's barbecue, she learns a lesson in tolerance.

the-simpsons.title: Treehouse of Horror VI
the-simpsons.description: In "Attack of the 50 Foot Eyesores," strange atmospheric conditions bring giant advertising statues to life. In "Nightmare on Evergreen Terrace," Groundskeeper Willie is killed in a freak accident and seeks revenge in the childrens' dreams. In the final segment, Homer steps through a secret portal and becomes three-dimensional.

the-simpsons.title: King-Size Homer
the-simpsons.description: Homer tries to gain sixty pounds so he can stay home on disability. When he nearly causes a catastrophe at the plant, Homer reconsiders his plan.

the-simpsons.title: Mother Simpson
the-simpsons.description: Homer discovers that his mother is still alive, a former radical who is a fugitive from the law. When her old nemesis Burns spots her and tips off the FBI, she is forced to return to the underground.

the-simpsons.title: Sideshow Bob's Last Gleaming
the-simpsons.description: After Sideshow Bob escapes from prison, the Springfield Air Show is the setting for his ill-fated vendetta against television and Krusty the Clown.

the-simpsons.title: The Simpsons 138th Episode Spectacular
the-simpsons.description: Troy McClure hosts a behind-the-scenes look at the show, including clips of the series' beginnings as shorts on "The Tracy Ullman Show," Simpsons trivia questions, and unaired scenes from popular episodes.

the-simpsons.title: Marge Be Not Proud
the-simpsons.description: Nabbed for shoplifting, Bart manages to keep it a secret from the family... until it's time to have the family Christmas photo taken at the Try-N-Save.

the-simpsons.title: Team Homer
the-simpsons.description: Homer catches Mr. Burns in an ether-induced haze and asks for $500 for his bowling team. When Burns' head clears, he demands to join the team. Meanwhile, Bart's inflammatory T-shirt provokes Principal Skinner to require school uniforms.

the-simpsons.title: Two Bad Neighbors
the-simpsons.description: Homer resents being upstaged when former president George Bush moves into the neighborhood. After Bush spanks Bart, an all-out prank war ensues.

the-simpsons.title: Scenes from the Class Struggle in Springfield
the-simpsons.description: A chance encounter with a former classmate yields an invitation to the Springfield Country Club, where Marge tries to parlay a bargain basement Chanel suit into elevated social status for her family.

the-simpsons.title: Bart the Fink
the-simpsons.description: In a scheme to get Krusty's autograph, Bart sends him a check. When Krusty's offshore holding corporation endorses the check, his illegal tax shelter is exposed. In despair after the government auctions off his possessions, Krusty fakes his own death.

the-simpsons.title: Lisa the Iconoclast
the-simpsons.description: While researching into Jebediah Springfield's past for an essay, Lisa discovers that the town founder wasn't the hero that everyone thinks he was.

the-simpsons.title: Homer the Smithers
the-simpsons.description: Forced to take a vacation, Smithers needs to find a temporary replacement who won't outshine him. Homer seems the perfect choice until a sudden outburst forces Mr. Burns to assert his independence.

the-simpsons.title: The Day the Violence Died
the-simpsons.description: Bart meets the original animator who created Itchy, penniless some 70 years after the studio stole his idea. When Bart helps him sue for restitution, he unwittingly bankrupts Itchy & Scratchy.

the-simpsons.title: A Fish Called Selma
the-simpsons.description: Washed up and plagued by scandal, Troy McClure sees a marriage to Selma as his ticket back to success.

the-simpsons.title: Bart on the Road
the-simpsons.description: Bart creates a fake driver's license for himself and uses it to go on a spring break road trip with Milhouse, Nelson, and Martin. Meanwhile, Homer and Lisa bond after spending some quality time together at work.

the-simpsons.title: 22 Short Films About Springfield
the-simpsons.description: Bart and Milhouse wonder if anything interesting happens to the citizens of Springfield, which leads to a series of interconnected vignettes.

the-simpsons.title: Raging Abe Simpson and His Grumbling Grandson in 'The Curse of the Flying Hellfish'
the-simpsons.description: When a fellow veteran dies, Grandpa Simpson and Mr. Burns fight for buried WWII treasure as the only surviving members of their battalion.

the-simpsons.title: Much Apu About Nothing
the-simpsons.description: When Mayor Quimby uses immigrants as a political scapegoat, the Simpsons discover that Apu is an illegal immigrant.

the-simpsons.title: Homerpalooza
the-simpsons.description: To show his kids how hip he is, Homer takes Bart and Lisa to a music festival, where he earns himself a place in the sideshow by catching a cannonball with his belly.

the-simpsons.title: Summer of 4 Ft. 2
the-simpsons.description: On a family vacation, Lisa tries on a new identity to fit in with the other kids at the beach. Jealous, Bart reveals her true nerdiness to the group.

the-simpsons.title: Treehouse of Horror VII
the-simpsons.description: A Halloween trilogy. This time, Bart meets his "pure evil" Siamese twin; Lisa's science project attacks Bart; aliens Kang and Kodos invade as Clinton and Dole's replicas just before the 1996 Presidential election.

the-simpsons.title: You Only Move Twice
the-simpsons.description: In an idyllic planned community, Homer works for a new boss who has trouble with the government. Meanwhile, the rest of the family has difficulty dealing with the bucolic burg.

the-simpsons.title: The Homer They Fall
the-simpsons.description: When Moe sees that Homer can absorb massive blows to the head, he turns him into a prizefighter and sets up a match with heavyweight champion Drederick Tatum.

the-simpsons.title: Burns, Baby Burns
the-simpsons.description: Mr. Burns' boorish long-lost son Larry gets the brush-off from Burns, but Homer hatches a plan to reconcile them.

the-simpsons.title: Bart After Dark
the-simpsons.description: After trespassing and damaging property at a mysterious old house, Bart is required to work there as a punishment... but it turns out to be a burlesque house.

the-simpsons.title: A Milhouse Divided
the-simpsons.description: Kirk and Luann Van Houten are getting a divorce. Homer is confident that it will never happen to him, but Kirk tells him how quickly things can change.

the-simpsons.title: Lisa's Date with Density
the-simpsons.description: Lisa develops a crush on Nelson and tries to change him into a better person. Meanwhile, Homer finds an autodialer and starts a telemarketing scam.

the-simpsons.title: Hurricane Neddy
the-simpsons.description: A hurricane destroys the Flanders' home and they have to move into the church basement. The people of Springfield gather to rebuild their house, but when Ned sees the poor workmanship, he has a complete breakdown.

the-simpsons.title: El Viaje Misterioso de Nuestro Jomer (The Mysterious Voyage of Homer)
the-simpsons.description: After eating a dish laced with potent peppers during the chili cookoff, Homer has hallucinations where a mystical coyote urges him to find his soulmate.

the-simpsons.title: The Springfield Files
the-simpsons.description: Homer witnesses something out of this world in Springfield woods, but no one believes him -- not even FBI agents Fox Mulder and Dana Scully, who come to investigate the incident.

the-simpsons.title: The Twisted World of Marge Simpson
the-simpsons.description: Marge's new pretzel franchise is failing until Homer strikes a deal with Fat Tony, Springfield's local mobster.

the-simpsons.title: Mountain of Madness
the-simpsons.description: To promote teamwork amongst the power plant's employees, Mr. Burns makes them go on a corporate retreat up in the mountains.

the-simpsons.title: Simpsoncalifragilisticexpiala (Annoyed Grunt) cious
the-simpsons.description: Marge is stressed by the demands of motherhood and the Simpsons get a magical British nanny, who floats down from the sky holding an umbrella.

the-simpsons.title: The Itchy & Scratchy & Poochie Show
the-simpsons.description: In an attempt to boost ratings, the Itchy and Scratchy Show adds a new "in-your-face" character voiced by Homer.

the-simpsons.title: Homer's Phobia
the-simpsons.description: The Simpsons befriend a shop owner, but when Homer discovers the man is gay, he worries about his influence on Bart.

the-simpsons.title: Brother from Another Series
the-simpsons.description: When Sideshow Bob is released from prison, his brother Cecil puts him in charge of building Springfield's new hydroelectric dam.

the-simpsons.title: My Sister, My Sitter
the-simpsons.description: Lisa has a stellar reputation as a babysitter, but when Homer and Marge leave her in charge of Bart and Maggie, everything starts going wrong.

the-simpsons.title: Homer vs. the Eighteenth Amendment
the-simpsons.description: When Prohibition is revived in Springfield, Homer and Bart supply the town with alcohol.

the-simpsons.title: Grade School Confidential
the-simpsons.description: Bart discovers Principal Skinner and Mrs. Krabappel kissing, and it's not long before the whole town knows of their secret affair.

the-simpsons.title: The Canine Mutiny
the-simpsons.description: When Bart can't pay the credit card bill for his expensive new purebred dog, the repo men unwittingly take Santa's Little Helper.

the-simpsons.title: The Old Man and the Lisa
the-simpsons.description: Financially ruined, Mr. Burns turns to Lisa for help in building a recycling business. Lisa believes he's changed, but his new business venture takes a shocking new direction.

the-simpsons.title: In Marge We Trust
the-simpsons.description: Disturbed that Reverend Lovejoy has lost interest in counseling parishioners, Marge volunteers as the "Listen Lady." Meanwhile, Homer sees his likeness on a box of Japanese detergent.

the-simpsons.title: Homer's Enemy
the-simpsons.description: A hardworking new employee at the power plant is consumed with resentment at Homer's undeserved success.

the-simpsons.title: The Simpsons Spin-Off Showcase
the-simpsons.description: Troy McClure presents three Simpsons spinoff spoofs: In "Chief Wiggum, P.I.," Chief Wiggum becomes a New Orleans detective. Next, Grampa Simpson's soul is trapped inside Moe's Love tester machine in "The Love-Matic Grampa." Finally, the Simpson family hosts a '70s-style variety show.

the-simpsons.title: The Secret War of Lisa Simpson
the-simpsons.description: Lisa joins the all-male military school where Bart is sent for discipline. Then comes the hazing.

the-simpsons.title: The City of New York vs. Homer Simpson
the-simpsons.description: Designated driver Barney absconds to Manhattan in Homer's car and leaves it there. But when the family journeys to the Big Apple to retrieve their property, Homer discovers his car has been booted.

the-simpsons.title: The Principal and the Pauper
the-simpsons.description: Unmasked as an impostor, Principal Skinner flees to Capital City to reclaim his former life as a shiftless good-for-nothing. The people of Springfield gain a newfound appreciation for him and form a plan to bring him back.

the-simpsons.title: Lisa's Sax
the-simpsons.description: After Lisa’s saxophone is destroyed, the Simpsons reminisce about how she originally got the instrument. On the hottest day of the year, Homer must decide whether to buy an air conditioner or replace Lisa’s sax.

the-simpsons.title: Treehouse of Horror VIII
the-simpsons.description: In “The Homega Man,” Homer faces a post-apocalyptic Springfield. Next, Bart attempts to become Superfly in "Fly vs. Fly." In “Easy-Bake Coven,” amidst a witch hunt in 1649, Marge and her sisters invent trick-or-treating.

the-simpsons.title: The Cartridge Family
the-simpsons.description: Alarmed by a soccer riot, Homer buys a handgun. His reckless behavior drives Marge and the kids out of the house, and even his new gun club buddies desert him.

the-simpsons.title: Bart Star
the-simpsons.description: When Homer becomes the coach of a peewee football team, he replaces star quarterback Nelson with the less talented Bart. Facing his teammates’ scorn, Bart looks for a way out but finds a better way to show his team spirit.

the-simpsons.title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
the-simpsons.description: Trying to escape his arranged marriage, Apu asks Marge to pose as his wife during his mother’s visit. When the ruse fails, Homer makes a last-ditch attempt to intervene, but Apu is smitten with his new bride Manjula.

the-simpsons.title: Lisa the Skeptic
the-simpsons.description: When a skeleton is unearthed at the site of a future shopping mall, all Springfield is convinced it is the skeleton of an angel – except Lisa.

the-simpsons.title: Realty Bites
the-simpsons.description: When Marge gets her real estate license, she learns to put a positive spin on the flaws of the houses she’s selling. But when the Flanders buy the Murder House, she realizes she has to tell the truth.

the-simpsons.title: Miracle on Evergreen Terrace
the-simpsons.description: After accidentally ruining the family’s Christmas tree and presents, Bart buries the evidence and claims a burglar stole everything. When Kent Brockman does a human interest story on the family’s tragic loss, the townspeople shower the family with generosity… until the truth comes out.

the-simpsons.title: All Singing, All Dancing
the-simpsons.description: Homer rents a Clint Eastwood movie and is dismayed to find it's a musical. Using clips from past episodes, the rest of the family reminds him about the many times he and other members of the family and town have broken into song and dance.

the-simpsons.title: Bart Carny
the-simpsons.description: When the carnival comes to town, Homer and Bart wind up working the ring toss. A father-son team of grifters shows them the downside of the “carny code,” but the Simpsons beat them at their own game.

the-simpsons.title: The Joy of Sect
the-simpsons.description: A cult lures in most of Springfield to toil for “The Leader.” After Marge escapes and has the family deprogrammed, Homer exposes the man behind the spaceship.

the-simpsons.title: Das Bus
the-simpsons.description: When Otto drives the school bus off a bridge, the kids wind up on a deserted island, fending for themselves in a “Lord of the Flies” parody. Back in Springfield, Homer takes on Bill Gates.

the-simpsons.title: The Last Temptation of Krust
the-simpsons.description: Krusty bombs at a charity comedy event and feels like a tired old hack. With the Simpsons’ support, Krusty takes his act in a fresh new direction… but in the end, his true nature asserts itself.

the-simpsons.title: Dumbbell Indemnity
the-simpsons.description: Moe goes broke trying to wine and dine a new girlfriend. Desperate for money, he cooks up an insurance scam with Homer.

the-simpsons.title: Lisa the Simpson
the-simpsons.description: Lisa struggles with solving a simple puzzle and fears that the "Simpson gene” is suddenly wiping out her intelligence. Homer stages a family reunion in hopes of introducing Lisa to some Simpsons she can respect.

the-simpsons.title: This Little Wiggy
the-simpsons.description: At Marge’s insistence, Bart has a “play date” with Ralph. Bart suddenly sees the upside of this friendship when he discovers Chief Wiggum’s “master key” and goes to explore Springfield’s abandoned prison.

the-simpsons.title: Simpson Tide
the-simpsons.description: When Homer joins the Naval Reserve, a captain takes a liking to him and leaves him in charge of a nuclear submarine.

the-simpsons.title: The Trouble with Trillions
the-simpsons.description: Facing an IRS audit, Homer agrees to help the feds bust Mr. Burns for a missing trillion-dollar bill. When Burns makes an anti-government stand, Homer flees with him to Cuba.

the-simpsons.title: Girly Edition
the-simpsons.description: Lisa becomes the anchor of a kids’ news program but is upstaged by Bart’s treacly human interest stories. At home, Homer corrupts a helper monkey.

the-simpsons.title: Trash of the Titans
the-simpsons.description: Homer feuds with the Springfield garbage men and decides to run for Sanitation Commissioner. After winning the election with a sleazy campaign, Homer can’t keep the extravagant promises he made to the town.

the-simpsons.title: King of the Hill
the-simpsons.description: After Rainier Wolfcastle helps Homer get in shape, Homer accepts a challenge to climb the Murderhorn, the tallest mountain in Springfield.

the-simpsons.title: Lost Our Lisa
the-simpsons.description: Bart’s latest stunt thwarts Lisa’s plan to attend a museum exhibit. When she tries to go alone and takes the wrong bus, Homer sets out to find her.

the-simpsons.title: Natural Born Kissers
the-simpsons.description: Homer and Marge try to spice up their love life and are caught baring it all in public. Bart and Lisa discover an alternate ending to Casablanca.

the-simpsons.title: Lard of the Dance
the-simpsons.description: Homer and Bart try to make money by selling used grease. Meanwhile, Lisa organizes a school dance but feels alienated when a new classmate and her friends try to act like adults.

the-simpsons.title: The Wizard of Evergreen Terrace
the-simpsons.description: A midlife crisis prompts Homer to quit his job and become an inventor.

the-simpsons.title: Bart the Mother
the-simpsons.description: Under Nelson's bad influence, Bart shoots a bird with a BB gun. Stricken with remorse, he tries to nurture the eggs from the bird's nest, which hatch into a species of lizard outlawed in Springfield.

the-simpsons.title: Treehouse of Horror IX
the-simpsons.description: In "Hell Toupée," Snake is sent to the electric chair, and his hair is transplanted onto Homer. In "The Terror of Tiny Toon," Bart and Lisa become cartoon characters in an episode of Itchy & Scratchy. In "Starship Poopers," a growth spurt casts doubt on Maggie's paternity, and the family goes on the Jerry Springer show.

the-simpsons.title: When You Dish Upon a Star
the-simpsons.description: After a chance encounter with Hollywood celebrities secretly living in Springfield, Homer becomes their friend and gofer... until he spills the beans to the gang at Moe's.

the-simpsons.title: D'oh-in' in the Wind
the-simpsons.description: In a quest to learn Homer's middle name, Homer and Grandpa travel to his mother's old commune, where Homer embraces the hippie life.

the-simpsons.title: Lisa Gets an 'A'
the-simpsons.description: Stuck at home with a cold, Lisa gets addicted to a video game and neglects her homework. Her A+++ on a test wins the school a grant, but when she confesses that she cheated, Skinner covers it up. Meanwhile, Homer raises a lobster.

the-simpsons.title: Homer Simpson in: 'Kidney Trouble'
the-simpsons.description: When Grandpa needs a new kidney, Homer agrees to donate one, but then chickens out.

the-simpsons.title: Mayored to the Mob
the-simpsons.description: After a riot at a sci-fi convention, Mayor Quimby hires Homer as his bodyguard, and Homer witnesses the rampant corruption in town politics. When Homer takes a stand, he runs afoul of the Springfield mafia.

the-simpsons.title: Viva Ned Flanders
the-simpsons.description: When clean-living Ned Flanders wants to experience a new side of life, Homer takes him to Las Vegas. After a drunken binge, they marry a pair of cocktail waitresses.

the-simpsons.title: Wild Barts Can't Be Broken
the-simpsons.description: Scapegoated for the vandalism of drunken Isotopes fans, the children of Springfield wage war on the adults by broadcasting their secrets on the radio.

the-simpsons.title: Sunday, Cruddy Sunday
the-simpsons.description: Homer and his friends charter a bus to the Super Bowl, only to find that their tickets are fake. Misadventures ensue.

the-simpsons.title: Homer to the Max
the-simpsons.description: A new TV series features a suave and debonair character named Homer Simpson. Homer capitalizes on his new namesake, until the character is rewritten to be a bumbling fool. Trying to recapture the positive attention he enjoyed, Homer changes his name to "Max Power."

the-simpsons.title: I'm with Cupid
the-simpsons.description: Apu is making the husbands of Springfield look bad with his extravagent Valentine's Day efforts for Manjula. When the men try to sabotage Apu's grand gesture, they accidentally wind up benefiting from it.

the-simpsons.title: Marge Simpson in: 'Screaming Yellow Honkers'
the-simpsons.description: A new Canyonero SUV turns timid Marge into an aggressive driver, and her road rage lands her in traffic school. But when a stampede occurs at the zoo, the town looks to Marge to save the day.

the-simpsons.title: Make Room for Lisa
the-simpsons.description: Indebted from a mishap at the Smithsonian, Homer lets a cell phone company put a transmitter in the house. Forced to share a room with Bart, Lisa resents Homer until a New Age experience gives her empathy.

the-simpsons.title: Maximum Homerdrive
the-simpsons.description: After beating Homer in a steak-eating competition, a trucker dies; Homer and Bart take over his rig to complete his shipment.

the-simpsons.title: Simpsons Bible Stories
the-simpsons.description: When Reverend Lovejoy subjects the congregation to an extended Bible reading, the Simpsons fall asleep and have dreams based on Bible stories.

the-simpsons.title: Mom and Pop Art
the-simpsons.description: Homer's failed do-it-yourself project gets mistaken for "outsider art." Suddenly in the limelight, Homer must come up with new "works" to impress the art world.

the-simpsons.title: The Old Man and the 'C' Student
the-simpsons.description: When Bart ruins Springfield's chance to host the Olympics, the kids are sentenced to community service work at the retirement home. To help the residents recapture their youth, Bart takes them on an ill-fated boat ride.

the-simpsons.title: Monty Can't Buy Me Love
the-simpsons.description: A new mogul wins the hearts of the townspeople with a shower of cash. Jealous, Mr. Burns asks Homer to help make him a beloved billionaire too, and they hatch a plan to bring the Loch Ness Monster to Springfield.

the-simpsons.title: They Saved Lisa's Brain
the-simpsons.description: Mayor Quimby flees Springfield, leaving the town chapter of Mensa in charge. As the group's new power goes to their heads, they take their utopian plans too far and the townspeople revolt.

the-simpsons.title: Thirty Minutes Over Tokyo
the-simpsons.description: After their bank account is drained at a cyber-cafe, the Simpsons go on a disastrous low-budget trip to Japan, where they wind up as contestants on a humiliating game show.

the-simpsons.title: Beyond Blunderdome
the-simpsons.description: Homer befriends Mel Gibson just as Mel is completing a remake of Mr. Smith Goes To Washington. Homer convinces Mel to make the film more violent, with disastrous results.

the-simpsons.title: Brother's Little Helper
the-simpsons.description: When Bart commits an extremely destructive prank, he is given Focusyn, a pill to help him concentrate in school. At first the results are impressive, and then Bart starts believing in a conspiracy involving spy satellites and major league baseball.

the-simpsons.title: Guess Who's Coming to Criticize Dinner?
the-simpsons.description: With Lisa's help, Homer uses his vast knowledge of food to become the town's leading restaurant critic. But when he gets petty and vindictive in his criticisms, all the other chefs in town try to kill him.

the-simpsons.title: Treehouse of Horror X
the-simpsons.description: In "I Know What You Diddily-Iddly-Did" the Simpsons fear they have killed Ned Flanders. "Desperately Xeeking Xena" satirizes superheroes of yore with "Stretch Dude" Bart and "Clobber Girl" Lisa. And "Life's A Glitch, Then You Die" depicts the upcoming horror of Y2K.

the-simpsons.title: E-I-E-I-(Annoyed Grunt)
the-simpsons.description: Fleeing from a duel, Homer takes his family to live on a farm. There he discovers that by mixing tomatoes, tobacco and radioactivity from the nuclear plant, he can create a dangerously delicious new substance.

the-simpsons.title: Hello Gutter, Hello Fadder
the-simpsons.description: Homer bowls a perfect 300 game, then concludes that the greatest accomplishment of his life is behind him. He reconnects with the world by bonding with baby Maggie.

the-simpsons.title: Eight Misbehavin'
the-simpsons.description: Due to overuse of fertility medication, Apu and wife Manjula give birth to octuplets. Desperate for money, Apu loans the babies to an unscrupulous carny promoter, then needs Homer's help to get them back.

the-simpsons.title: Take My Wife, Sleaze
the-simpsons.description: After winning a motorcycle at a dance contest, Homer becomes part of a motorcycle gang. But when he puts Marge's photo in a biker magazine, a much tougher gang takes her, and he must win her back.

the-simpsons.title: Grift of the Magi
the-simpsons.description: In this Christmas-themed episode, the students of Springfield Elementary are unwittingly used as a focus group to test new toys. The product of their labors, a cuddly doll named Funzo, is a lot more sinister than he appears.

the-simpsons.title: Little Big Mom
the-simpsons.description: When Marge leaves the house to recuperate from a skating injury, everything goes to hell - until Lisa convinces Homer and Bart they have leprosy.

the-simpsons.title: Faith Off
the-simpsons.description: Homer gets a bucket stuck on his head, and when it is removed the town is convinced that Bart has the powers of a faith healer. Then mobster Fat Tony tries to turn the boy's spiritual abilities into more sinister directions.

the-simpsons.title: The Mansion Family
the-simpsons.description: Worried about his health, Mr. Burns visits the Mayo Clinic. He lets Homer housesit his mansion, which leads of course to an offshore knife fight and an attack by Chinese pirates.

the-simpsons.title: Saddlesore Galactica
the-simpsons.description: Homer and Bart befriend a diving horse at a county fair. They turn it into a racehorse with an attitude, whose success runs them afoul of mysterious, tree-dwelling jockeys.

the-simpsons.title: Alone Again, Natura-Diddily
the-simpsons.description: Ned's wife Maude is inadvertently killed by a T-shirt accident at an auto race. Homer and his family try to help Ned cope.

the-simpsons.title: Missionary: Impossible
the-simpsons.description: When Homer fails to give money he promised over the phone, he is forced by PBS stars to flee the country. He becomes a missionary on a small tropical island, where he introduces the natives to casino gambling.

the-simpsons.title: Pygmoelian
the-simpsons.description: Plastic surgery gives Moe the bartender a handsome new face and a whole new life as a soap opera star.

the-simpsons.title: Bart to the Future
the-simpsons.description: We see a possible future in which Bart is a grown-up slacker, living with Ralph Wiggum, while Lisa is no less than President of the United States.

the-simpsons.title: Days of Wine and D'oh'ses
the-simpsons.description: After being embarrassed by a drunken video of himself, Barney vows to sober up. Newly clean, he gets work as a helicopter pilot.

the-simpsons.title: Kill the Alligator and Run
the-simpsons.description: After a terrible bout with insomnia, Homer takes the family to Florida during spring break. There, they kill a beloved alligator and are sentenced to a chain gang.

the-simpsons.title: Last Tap Dance in Springfield
the-simpsons.description: Lisa enters a tap dancing academy, where the teacher is a child star who never quite grew up. Meanwhile, Homer gets laser eye surgery.

the-simpsons.title: It's a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad Marge
the-simpsons.description: Otto's girlfriend seems to be usurping Marge's role when she moves in with the family after a dispute over heavy metal.

the-simpsons.title: Behind the Laughter
the-simpsons.description: A "Behind the Music"-style look at the Simpsons, narrated by VH1's Jim Forbes, shows their rise to stardom--and the "private hell" that followed.

the-simpsons.title: Treehouse of Horror XI
the-simpsons.description: This year's Halloween story sees The Simpsons as "The Munsters" (with everyone except Lisa getting killed), Homer as a wandering spirit on the hunt for a good deed in "G-G-Ghost D-D-Dad," Bart and Lisa as peasants in a fairy tale forest in "Scary Tales Can Come True," and Lisa inadvertently dooming mankind by rescuing a dolphin in "Night of the Dolphin."

the-simpsons.title: A Tale of Two Springfields
the-simpsons.description: While calling Animal Control over a badger taking residence in Santa's Little Helper's doghouse, Homer discovers that Springfield has two different area codes–and ends up leading a revolt that splits the town in two.

the-simpsons.title: Insane Clown Poppy
the-simpsons.description: Krusty takes parenting lessons from Homer when, during an outdoor book fair, a girl tells Krusty that she is his long-lost daughter from a one-night stand with a female soldier who fought during the first Gulf War.

the-simpsons.title: Lisa the Tree Hugger
the-simpsons.description: Lisa falls for the teenaged leader of a militant environmentalist group and tries to impress him by living in Springfield's oldest tree in order to keep it from being cut down.

the-simpsons.title: Homer vs. Dignity
the-simpsons.description: When the Simpsons once again have financial problems, Mr. Burns pays Homer to play pranks on others and humiliate himself in public. Meanwhile, Smithers creates a Malibu Stacy-themed musical.

the-simpsons.title: The Computer Wore Menace Shoes
the-simpsons.description: Homer decides to buy a computer after turning up to the Plant to find it closed by e-mail. He then creates his own website and it eventually gains attention when he posts gossip. Homer dubs himself as "Mr. X" to conceal his identity. When he reveals that he is Mr. X, he becomes drugged into a mysterious island where people who know too much are imprisoned after Homer starts writing conspiracy theories such as flu shots.

the-simpsons.title: The Great Money Caper
the-simpsons.description: Homer and Bart become father–son con artists (after Bart is given money out of pity when Homer decided to not take him home), but soon find that they are the ones being had.

the-simpsons.title: Skinner's Sense of Snow
the-simpsons.description: A snowstorm traps the students of Springfield Elementary inside, with them overthrowing Principal Skinner when he uses his Army skills to control them. Meanwhile, Homer tries to rescue the children–using Flanders' car.

the-simpsons.title: HOMЯ
the-simpsons.description: While working as a human guinea pig (to pay off the family's lost savings after making a bad investment), Homer discovers the root cause of his subnormal intelligence: a crayon that was lodged in his brain ever since he was a boy. He decides to have it removed to increase his IQ, but discovers that being smart does not necessarily equal being happy.

the-simpsons.title: Pokey Mom
the-simpsons.description: Marge tries to rehabilitate a convict with remarkable artistic talent. Meanwhile, Homer uses a trash can to fix people's spines.

the-simpsons.title: Worst Episode Ever
the-simpsons.description: Bart and Milhouse are banned from The Android Dungeon after stopping Comic Book Guy from buying a box of priceless Star Wars memorabilia for $5, but are hired as his replacements when Comic Book Guy has a heart attack and is advised to leave his job in order to make friends.

the-simpsons.title: Tennis the Menace
the-simpsons.description: While making funeral arrangements for Grampa's future, the funeral planner pitches the idea of a mausoleum that uses the same amount of cement as a full-sized tennis court. This prompts Homer to instead build a tennis court in his backyard, initially mistaking the sport for "Foxy Boxing". The tennis court makes Marge and Homer popular in town, but it turns out that this is only because Homer's inferior tennis ability makes them an easy target. Bart on the other hand, shines as a natural.

the-simpsons.title: Day of the Jackanapes
the-simpsons.description: Krusty announces his retirement due to interference from network executives and the growing popularity of the big-money game show "Me Wantee", but when Krusty reveals to Sideshow Bob that all of the episodes featuring him have been erased, Sideshow Bob uses Krusty's biggest fan (Bart) to murder him during Krusty's farewell show.

the-simpsons.title: New Kids on the Blecch
the-simpsons.description: A music producer selects Bart, Nelson, Milhouse and Ralph to be members of the next hit boy band, who record subliminal songs about joining the Navy.

the-simpsons.title: Hungry, Hungry Homer
the-simpsons.description: Homer becomes a Good Samaritan after discovering the simple joys of helping people in need–which is put to the test when he goes on a hunger strike after the owner of the Springfield Isotopes attempts to discredit him when Homer stumbles on his plot to discreetly move the team to Albuquerque, New Mexico.

the-simpsons.title: Bye Bye Nerdie
the-simpsons.description: When Lisa becomes the target of a female bully, Lisa discovers a scientific reason as to why bullies pick on nerds. Meanwhile, Homer goes into the baby-proofing business, which is threatening the businesses of pediatricians and greeting card salesmen.

the-simpsons.title: Simpson Safari
the-simpsons.description: When the Simpsons run out of food thanks to a bag boy strike (caused by Homer), the family finds an old box of animal crackers with a sweepstakes that sends The Simpsons to Africa.

the-simpsons.title: Trilogy of Error
the-simpsons.description: Homer's rush to the hospital to reattach his thumb, Lisa's rush to school to win the science fair, and Bart's run-in with an illegal fireworks scheme are interconnected in a parody of Go and Run Lola Run.

the-simpsons.title: I'm Goin' to Praiseland
the-simpsons.description: After finding a sketchbook belonging to his late wife Maude, Ned Flanders opens a Bible-themed amusement park to honor her memory.

the-simpsons.title: Children of a Lesser Clod
the-simpsons.description: After spraining his knee during a basketball game, Homer begins taking care of the neighborhood kids to cure his boredom, prompting jealousy from Bart and Lisa, who feel that Homer is giving the kids the attention they never had.

the-simpsons.title: Simpsons Tall Tales
the-simpsons.description: When Homer refuses to pay a five dollar airport tax to fly to Delaware, the family is forced to ride in a livestock car of a train instead. There they meet a singing hobo who tells three tall tales:  Homer as Paul Bunyan.  Lisa as Connie Appleseed, a parody of Johnny Appleseed.  Bart as Tom Sawyer with Nelson as Huckleberry Finn.

the-simpsons.title: Treehouse of Horror XII
the-simpsons.description:
In the twelfth Treehouse of Horror episode:

Hex and the City – While on a day trip through Ethnictown, Homer's bumbling catches the ire of a gypsy, who curses Homer's family and friends into receiving nothing but bad luck.

House of Whacks – in this mixed parody of Demon Seed and 2001: A Space Odyssey, Marge buys an automated house and customizes it with the Pierce Brosnan personality, who falls for Marge and attempts to murder Homer.

Wiz Kids – In this Harry Potter parody, Bart and Lisa go to a school for wizards, and Lord Montemort (Mr. Burns) uses Bart to capture Lisa's magic.

Guest star: Pierce Brosnan and Matthew Perry.[20]

the-simpsons.title: The Parent Rap
the-simpsons.description: Bart gets in trouble for joyriding in a police car, but feels confident he will be let off by Judge Snyder. However, Snyder goes on vacation before ruling his verdict and is replaced with a coldhearted judge named Constance Harm. She accuses Homer of being a negligent father and sentences him to be tethered to Bart. The two are against it at first but later start to bond. Marge however is unable to take anymore of it and slices the tether off of them both. Homer and Marge then go after Judge Harm only to end up sinking her houseboat. Eventually Bart decides to take punishment and is about to be sentenced to 5 year in juvenile hall, only though Judge Snyder returns and dismisses Harm.

the-simpsons.title: Homer the Moe
the-simpsons.description: Moe becomes depressed and decides to return to bartending school so he can re-evaluate himself. He meets an old teacher, who suggests that Moe try improving his bar, which might make him happier. Moe takes the advice, and turns his bar into a trendy nightclub, which does not sit well with his regular customers Homer, Lenny, Carl, and Barney.

the-simpsons.title: A Hunka Hunka Burns in Love
the-simpsons.description: Homer becomes a fortune cookie writer for a Chinatown restaurant. Mr. Burns reads one of Homer's fortunes, which says that the reader will find love before Flag Day is over. Burns goes searching for love and meets Gloria, a meter maid, and asks her out. Gloria reluctantly agrees, and Burns recruits Homer to help him look young and hip to his new girlfriend.

the-simpsons.title: The Blunder Years
the-simpsons.description: After tricking Marge into thinking an advertising spokesman is coming to visit her, Homer takes Marge and the rest of the family to a restaurant. A hypnotist uses his powers on Homer, and makes him remember a horrific childhood incident where Homer found a dead body in a ravine. The Simpson family decides to investigate this and find out where the body came from.

the-simpsons.title: She of Little Faith
the-simpsons.description: After Homer and Bart's model rocket damages the church, Mr. Burns makes a deal to commercialize the church in return for paying for the damages. Lisa becomes disgusted at what the church has become, so she decides to find a new religion suitable for her. She eventually converts to Buddhism, causing Marge to fear for Lisa's soul.

the-simpsons.title: Brawl in the Family
the-simpsons.description: A social worker is assigned to make the Simpson family functional after they get arrested for fighting while playing Monopoly. He helps them learn how to work together and function as a family. The moment is ruined when, Ginger and Amber, the barmaids who married Homer and Flanders while they were drunk in "Viva Ned Flanders", arrive at the Simpsons' home, which outrages Marge.

the-simpsons.title: Sweets and Sour Marge
the-simpsons.description: Springfield is officially declared the World's Fattest Town after an attempt to break a world record lands everyone on top of a truck scale. Out of embarrassment and disgust, Marge goes on a crusade against the local sugar corporation. However, when sugar is banned, Homer, Bart, Mr. Burns and Apu start bootlegging sugar.

the-simpsons.title: Jaws Wired Shut
the-simpsons.description: A jaw injury from colliding with a new town statue turns Homer into a better listener while recuperating with his jaws wired shut, but once the wires come off, Homer does not go back to being loud and obnoxious and Marge becomes starved for thrills.

the-simpsons.title: Half-Decent Proposal
the-simpsons.description: Homer develops a snoring problem, so Marge decides to spend a night with her sisters Patty and Selma. After a night of drinking, Marge sees a news report about her ex-prom date Artie Ziff, who is now very wealthy, and decides to send him an e-mail. Artie is still obsessed with Marge, so he offers the Simpsons $1 million in exchange for Marge spending a weekend with him.

the-simpsons.title: The Bart Wants What It Wants
the-simpsons.description: Bart befriends Rainer Wolfcastle's daughter Greta. She has a crush on Bart, but he does not seem to realize it and eventually stops seeing her. Seeking revenge, Greta begins dating Bart's best friend Milhouse, which causes Bart to start missing her. She leaves for Toronto with her father, and Bart convinces his family to follow them there.

the-simpsons.title: The Lastest Gun in the West
the-simpsons.description: While running away from a vicious dog, Bart meets Buck McCoy, a former Western film star. Bart begins hanging out with him and starts to idolize him. Bart wants to help McCoy stage a comeback, so he convinces all of the kids in town to become interested in the Wild West. McCoy appears on the Krusty the Clown Show, but the comeback flops when Buck begins drinking again and injures Krusty the Clown.

the-simpsons.title: The Old Man and the Key
the-simpsons.description: Grampa falls in love with Zelda, a woman who has an interest in men who can drive. He decides to get his driver's license back, but is ignorant to Homer and Marge's concerns that she is only using him for his car.

the-simpsons.title: Tales from the Public Domain
the-simpsons.description: When Homer gets a notice from the library that he has a book of classic tales that is years overdue, he finds it on the shelf and reads three stories: The Odyssey (where Homer and his bar buddies try to get home after fighting the Trojans), Joan of Arc (where Lisa leads the French against the English with the help of God), and Hamlet (where Bart tries to kill Moe after Moe kills Homer in order to marry Marge).

the-simpsons.title: Blame It on Lisa
the-simpsons.description: When Homer gets the family's telephone service cut off for refusing to pay for calls made to Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, Lisa confesses that she was the one who called Rio after sponsoring an orphan who goes missing. She convinces the family to travel to Brazil to look for him. However, once there, they have no luck finding him, and Homer is kidnapped.

the-simpsons.title: Weekend at Burnsie's
the-simpsons.description: Homer is prescribed medicinal marijuana after getting pecked in the eyes by a murder of crows. While his family and friends worry about the drug altering his personality, Homer becomes Mr. Burns's vice president after cracking up at Burns's antiquated jokes.

the-simpsons.title: Gump Roast
the-simpsons.description: In this clip show episode, Homer is honored at a Friars' Club Roast. A number of characters show up to roast him, but the celebrating is interrupted by Kang and Kodos, who say that humanity will be judged based on Homer's experiences.

the-simpsons.title: I Am Furious (Yellow)
the-simpsons.description: Inspired by a cartoonist who speaks at the school as part of a career day assembly, Bart creates a comic book series based on Homer and his anger problems, which turns into a popular Internet cartoon series called Angry Dad. Homer finds out about this and is at first outraged, but after talking to his family, he decides to try to become a less angry person.

the-simpsons.title: The Sweetest Apu
the-simpsons.description: Homer and Marge discover that Apu is having an affair with the Squishee delivery lady at the Kwik-E-Mart. They decide to keep Apu's wife Manjula from finding out about it. However, she eventually learns of Apu's affair by watching store security tapes. She throws Apu out of the house and decides to file for divorce, but soon realizes that she misses him.

the-simpsons.title: Little Girl in the Big Ten
the-simpsons.description: Lisa tries to fit in with two college students by lying about her age. She finds that the college atmosphere is perfect for her, but her lie is soon discovered and she is shunned by her fellow elementary school students. Meanwhile, Bart is diagnosed with a weakened immune system after getting bitten by a Chinese mosquito and must live in a plastic, germ-free bubble.

the-simpsons.title: The Frying Game
the-simpsons.description: While faced with community service for abusing an endangered insect, Homer begins assisting an elderly woman named Mrs. Bellamy. One night, Mrs. Bellamy is murdered, and Homer and Marge are accused of committing the crime.

the-simpsons.title: Poppa's Got a Brand New Badge
the-simpsons.description: Homer starts a security company with Lenny and Carl after the police are ineffective during a blackout, and eventually Mayor Quimby decides to have them replace the police. Homer finds that he excels at the job, but then he runs afoul of mob boss Fat Tony, who threatens Homer with death unless he leaves town.

the-simpsons.title: Treehouse of Horror XIII
the-simpsons.description:
The 13th Treehouse of Horror episode, consisting of three self-contained segments.

Send in the Clones – Homer buys a hammock that can produce clones of himself. He creates numerous clones to help him around the house, but they soon overrun Springfield.

The Fright to Creep and Scare Harms – Lisa petitions the town to get rid of their firearms after discovering the gravestone of a young man named William Bonney who died from gun violence. However, Lisa soon discovers that William Bonney is the real name of Western outlaw Billy the Kid, whose ghost, along with the ghosts of other infamous criminals, takes over the defenseless town.

The Island of Dr. Hibbert – Dr. Hibbert invites the citizens of Springfield to his island resort, where he turns them into animals.

the-simpsons.title: How I Spent My Strummer Vacation
the-simpsons.description: A drunken Homer appears on the show Taxicab Conversations and rants about how awful his life as a husband and father is. Although his family is at first outraged, they realise that they do somewhat burden him and decide to make up for it by sending him to a Rock 'n Roll Fantasy Camp where he mingles with rock stars, including Mick Jagger and Keith Richards. The rock stars ask Homer to help out at a concert and, expecting that he will be allowed to perform, he accepts. Actually, they want him to test the microphones; however, a humiliated Homer grabs a guitar and starts playing.

the-simpsons.title: Bart vs. Lisa vs. the Third Grade
the-simpsons.description: The Simpsons buy a satellite television, which Bart spends so much time watching that he does not study for an important achievement test. He scores so low that Principal Skinner demotes him to third grade, while Lisa does so well that she is moved up to third grade. The two are placed in the same class and become rivals. During a trip to Capital City, they get separated from their class and are forced to help each other in order to find their classmates.

the-simpsons.title: Large Marge
the-simpsons.description: Thinking Homer does not find her attractive anymore, Marge decides to get liposuction, but instead receives breast implants. She becomes adored by many of the men in Springfield, and becomes a spokesmodel for trade shows. Meanwhile, Bart and Milhouse try to imitate a stunt they saw on an episode of Batman that guest stars Krusty the Clown. When the stunt ends badly, media watchdog groups blame Krusty, forcing the clown to make his show more safety-conscious and less fun.

the-simpsons.title: Helter Shelter
the-simpsons.description: The Simpson family has to find temporary residence while their house is fumigated for termites. When they run out of options, they decide to become contestants on a reality show where families live in the manner that people did in 1895. The family is initially miserable, but slowly adapt to their new life, which causes the show to lose ratings. The producers decide to try to boost viewers by dumping the house in a river and forcing the family to survive in the wilderness. However, the Simpsons find a bunch of rejects from other reality shows and they attack the producers.

the-simpsons.title: The Great Louse Detective
the-simpsons.description: The Simpson family win a free spa weekend, and Homer is nearly killed when a mysterious figure locks him in a sauna. Chief Wiggum decides to hire someone who can think like a murderer in order to find one. Bart's mortal enemy Sideshow Bob is sent to live with the Simpsons so he can help find Homer's attempted killer. Bob and Homer track down the attempted murderer and discover that it is Frank Grimes, Jr., the son of a man that Homer drove to insanity (in the season eight episode "Homer's Enemy"). After Grimes is arrested, Bob tries to kill Bart, but he finds that he has "grown accustomed to [his] face" and cannot harm him.

the-simpsons.title: Special Edna
the-simpsons.description: Ms. Edna Krabappel begins to lose faith in her relationship with Principal Skinner and becomes depressed. Bart wants to cheer her up and decides to nominate her for the Teacher of the Year Award. Ms. Krabappel and the Simpsons are given a free trip to Epcot Center in Orlando, Florida. Skinner decides that he needs to do something to win Edna back, so he follows them there. He tries to sabotage Edna's chances of winning the award, in hopes that she will become so depressed that she will come back to him. However, he has a change of heart and proposes to her.

the-simpsons.title: The Dad Who Knew Too Little
the-simpsons.description: Homer hires a private detective to learn more about Lisa. But when Homer refuses to pay the detective's expenses, he frames Lisa for a crime she didn't commit, forcing her and Homer to go on the run.

the-simpsons.title: The Strong Arms of the Ma
the-simpsons.description: Marge gets mugged and becomes so traumatized that she develops Agoraphobia. She hides in the basement. Having little else to do, she decides to exercise with a weight set Homer bought from Rainier Wolfcastle's garage sale. She becomes so strong and confident that she is able to leave the basement. She continues working out and decides to start taking steroids so she can enter a bodybuilding competition. One night at Moe's Tavern she loses her temper and starts destroying the bar and fighting all of the patrons. Homer confronts Marge and says he misses the sweet woman that he married. Marge, horrified at what she has done, apologizes and decides to stop working out.

the-simpsons.title: Pray Anything
the-simpsons.description: Homer becomes depressed when he sees that Ned Flanders seems to be better off than him. To remedy this, he begins to pray constantly. Meanwhile, the Simpsons discover that tree roots have clogged up their plumbing. The house becomes too run down to live in, and Homer prays for a solution. Homer is injured while attending church; he sues Reverend Lovejoy and is awarded the deed to the church. He throws a huge house-warming party, in which all of the partiers drink and engage in sinful activities. It suddenly starts raining and the town begins to flood. The townspeople flee to the roof of the church. Homer tries praying again but the flood keeps rising. Reverend Lovejoy returns in a helicopter and leads everyone in prayer, asking God to forgive them, and the rain stops.

the-simpsons.title: Barting Over
the-simpsons.description: Bart learns that he was once a child actor in commercials and that all the money earned was spent by Homer. In retaliation, Bart petitions the court to have himself legally emancipated from his parents and moves out of the Simpson house. Bart is initially miserable in his new apartment, but discovers that skateboarder Tony Hawk lives on one of the floors above. He and Hawk become friends, and Bart is content with his new life. Homer apologizes to Bart and requests that he return home. Bart accepts the apology, but tells his family that he is going on tour with Hawk. At an event, Homer speaks to Bart and finally promises Bart that he will never treat him badly again.

the-simpsons.title: I'm Spelling as Fast as I Can
the-simpsons.description: Lisa competes at a spelling bee and earns the right to compete in the Spell-lympics, becoming the pride of the town. The host of the show George Plimpton, asks her to intentionally lose so that a more popular boy can win. Lisa refuses and continues to compete, but accidentally misspells a word and loses. Meanwhile, Homer tours with a group obsessed with eating Krusty Burger's latest sandwich.

the-simpsons.title: A Star is Born-Again
the-simpsons.description: During the annual Jellyfish Festival, Ned Flanders realizes that he is lonely and becomes depressed. One night, he meets a beautiful woman, who asks him out on a date. He soon learns that the woman is Sara Sloan, a famous actress. Sloan is charmed by Flanders' wholesomeness, and they continue to date to the point at which she asks that he move to Hollywood. Flanders, worried that Hollywood would conflict with his conservative Christian values, refuses, so Sloan instead decides to stay in Springfield. However, their relationship does not work out, due to his insistence on marriage.

the-simpsons.title: Mr. Spritz Goes to Washington
the-simpsons.description: An air traffic route is redirected so that airplanes start flying directly over the Simpsons' house. The noise starts to disrupt their lives and, desperate for a solution, the family turns to their Congressman. However, he dies of a heart attack, so they ask Krusty the Clown to run for Congress so that he can help them. Krusty is successful in his campaign, but finds that his air traffic bill is ignored by the veteran Congressmen. He soon becomes disillusioned with the system, so the Simpsons, with guidance from Walter Mondale, help him out by blackmailing one of his opponents and attaching the bill to a more popular one. The bill passes, and the air traffic is re-routed.

the-simpsons.title: C. E. D'oh
the-simpsons.description: Homer decides to try for a promotion at Springfield Nuclear Power Plant and suggests several ideas to Mr. Burns, all of which are rejected. One night, Homer overhears Burns admit that the plant's real owner is a canary to protect Burns from responsibility for any wrongdoing by the power plant. Homer releases the bird and tells Burns that nuclear inspectors have arrived for a surprise inspection. Burns, desperate to find a scapegoat, names Homer the new owner. As his first act, Homer fires Burns and takes control of the Plant. However, he finds that his work life as a CEO is conflicting with his family life. Homer decides to return to his old job and gives ownership back to Burns.

the-simpsons.title: 'Scuse Me While I Miss the Sky
the-simpsons.description: A snobby British filmmaker named Declan Desmond begins making a documentary about student life at Springfield Elementary School. When introduced to Lisa, he tells her that she has too many goals and suggests that she pick one career. Lisa focuses on astronomy, but cannot watch the stars because of light pollution. She convinces Mayor Quimby to decrease the light's intensity during the night, which only results in an increase in the crime rate. Quimby bows to public pressure and switches the lights back on permanently. Lisa overloads the generators at the Power Plant, causing a power outage, and is able to watch a meteor shower undisturbed by light.

the-simpsons.title: Three Gays of the Condo
the-simpsons.description: After yet another Homer and Marge fight, Homer ends up sharing a condo with two homosexuals - who don't exactly think Homer is straight.

the-simpsons.title: Dude, Where's My Ranch?
the-simpsons.description: When challenged to think up a new Christmas carol, Homer instead writes a song about how much he hates Ned Flanders. The song becomes such a hit that the Simpsons become sick of hearing it and take a trip to a dude ranch. Lisa develops affections for a local boy named Luke but becomes jealous when he hears him talking to a girl named Clara on the telephone. One night, she meets Clara and gives her the wrong directions, leading her to become lost. After Lisa discovers that Clara is actually Luke's sister, she rushes to find her. She saves Clara, and decides to tell Luke what happened, but he is offended and dumps her. Meanwhile, Bart and Homer decide to help a tribe of Native Americans who want a beaver dam removed so they can reclaim their land.

the-simpsons.title: Old Yeller-Belly
the-simpsons.description: Homer throws out Santa's Little Helper for not saving him from a fire, but soon the dog becomes Duff's new mascot.

the-simpsons.title: Brake My Wife, Please
the-simpsons.description: Homer becomes obsessed with using new gadgets in his car. One day, he becomes distracted and drives off a pier, losing his driver's license. Unable to use a car, Homer starts to learn the joys of walking. Meanwhile, Marge shoulders the burden of Homer's driving duties and becomes stressed out. One day, as Homer sings about the virtues of walking, Marge accidentally runs him over with her car. Later, as Homer recuperates from the accident, he begins to suspect that Marge is trying to hurt him. They fight and go to see a marriage counselor. The counselor advises Homer to perform one completely unselfish gesture to win Marge back. Homer holds a party with all of her friends and a surprised Marge tells Homer that she loves him.

the-simpsons.title: The Bart of War
the-simpsons.description: After destroying Flanders' shrine to The Beatles, Bart and Milhouse are punished by being put in community groups. Bart joins the Pre-Teen Braves along with Ralph Wiggum, Nelson Muntz and Database. Led by Marge, they start engaging in community activities. However, they soon become rivals with The Cavalry Kids, led by Milhouse. The two groups try to outdo each other and become involved in a contest to sell the most candy. The Cavalry Kids win the prize of singing the national anthem at a baseball game. However, the Pre-Teen Braves pretend to be The Cavalry Kids and sing their own version of the national anthem. As the crowd becomes enraged, the real Cavalry Kids arrive and a massive stadium-wide brawl erupts. Marge becomes upset, and the fighting ends when an image of her crying is shown on the JumboTron.

the-simpsons.title: Moe Baby Blues
the-simpsons.description: Moe Szyslak becomes lonely and decides to commit suicide by jumping off a bridge. However, he inadvertently saves Maggie Simpson when she is sent flying from the Simpsons' car window and into his arms. He starts playing with Maggie and becomes attached to her, telling her the story of The Godfather. Homer and Marge become upset about how much time Moe is spending with Maggie and forbid him from seeing her again. One night, Maggie wakes up and hears Fat Tony and the Springfield Mafia outside the house and decides to follow them. When Homer and Marge find her missing, they automatically assume that Moe kidnapped her. When Moe is told that Maggie is missing, his request to help find her is granted by Homer. Maggie follows the mobsters to Luigi's restaurant, where Fat Tony's gang gets into a gun battle with a rival family. Homer, Marge and Moe track Maggie down and Moe decides to go inside and save Maggie. After Moe saves Maggie's life, Homer allows the two to spend more time together.

the-simpsons.title: Treehouse of Horror XIV
the-simpsons.description: "Reaper Madness" - Death becomes Homer and our hero must learn to reap what he sows (and pull a fast one on the almighty). "Frinkenstein" - Soon to be Nobel-prize winning Professor Frink reanimates his father for some gruesome body parts-swapping. "Stop the World, I Want to Goof Off" - A parody of Clockstoppers, starring Bart and Milhouse.

the-simpsons.title: My Mother the Carjacker
the-simpsons.description: Homer's mother returns, and after being cleared of all charges, is re-imprisoned on a technicality.

the-simpsons.title: The President Wore Pearls
the-simpsons.description: In this loose parody of the musical/movie Evita, Lisa is elected Student Body president, but is unaware that the school staff is using her for their own devices and as a scapegoat if something goes wrong.

the-simpsons.title: The Regina Monologues
the-simpsons.description: After making over $3000 from his own museum featuring a $1000 bill, Bart takes the family to London (on the suggestion of Grampa), where Homer is arrested for treason after crashing into the Queen.

the-simpsons.title: The Fat and the Furriest
the-simpsons.description: Homer is humiliated when he appears on the news running from a bear that nearly attacks him at the city dump. After Grampa scolds him, he swears to fight the bear himself.

the-simpsons.title: Today I Am a Clown
the-simpsons.description: Krusty discovers that he never had a bar mitzvah as a child. He quits his show to have it as an adult, with the help of his father, Rabbi Krustofski. Meanwhile, Homer hosts a late-night talk show a la "Politically Incorrect with Bill Maher" as a replacement for Krusty's show.

the-simpsons.title: 'Tis the Fifteenth Season
the-simpsons.description: Homer realizes how selfish he is after he spends all the family's Christmas money on a present for himself. He becomes the nicest guy in town, making Ned Flanders jealous.

the-simpsons.title: Marge vs. Singles, Seniors, Childless Couples and Teens, and Gays
the-simpsons.description: When a group of singles, seniors, childless couples, teens and gays band together to protest having to accommodate families (including paying property taxes used to teach children they do not have) after a riot at a children's concert, Marge takes up the cause for the families, with some help from Bart and Lisa.

the-simpsons.title: I, (Annoyed Grunt)-Bot
the-simpsons.description: Homer builds a battle robot to win Bart's respect, and places it in a tournament against other robots. What Bart does not know, though, is that the robot is actually Homer in costume. Meanwhile, Snowball II dies and Lisa tries to find a replacement cat.

the-simpsons.title: Diatribe of a Mad Housewife
the-simpsons.description: Marge writes a romance novel with characters based on Homer and Ned Flanders that becomes a hit. Meanwhile, Homer gets fired from the power plant again and becomes an ambulance driver.

the-simpsons.title: Margical History Tour
